headline: Typhoon Dujuan kills four in Japan; White House launches 24/7 “Trump TV”; Google backs Georgia nuclear uprates.

stories.title: Typhoon Dujuan: four dead as storm lashes Tokyo region
facts: BBC: four dead after Typhoon Dujuan battered Tokyo and surrounding prefectures with torrential rain and destructive winds; six others reported missing (NHK).
At the peak Monday, authorities warned of an “imminent threat to life” and urged about 1.9 million people toward shelters; most evacuation orders lifted Tuesday as the storm moved offshore.
Power cut for ~50,000 people; hundreds of flights suspended; Tokyo Game Show cancelled Monday’s programme; Rock in Japan concerts cancelled.
Fatalities tied to landslides in Kanagawa and Chiba; Japan Times also reports at least four dead and six missing in Kanto; CNA notes ~45,000 houses without power.
Sustained winds ~130 km/h with gusts to ~194 km/h; Japan’s 25th typhoon of the year during a holiday stretch.
stories.whyItMatters: The clearest overnight human-impact story — landslides and mass shelter orders around Tokyo, with transport and major events knocked offline as leaders head into UNGA week.

stories.title: White House launches 24/7 “Trump TV” YouTube stream
facts: heise (dpa): amid the fight with CNN, MS NOW and Politico over White House access, the administration launched a round-the-clock “Trump TV” stream of “essential” government moments.
Early feed mixed Trump speeches with U.S. military exercise footage and commentary; little original production at first; available on YouTube.
TV pool partners (Fox, ABC, CBS, NBC, CNN) had suspended the shared pool — leaving a White House press event with Trump hard to hear on the official livestream Monday.
n-tv frames the launch as the administration’s answer in the media dispute.
stories.whyItMatters: A direct distribution channel past the traditional TV pool — timed to an access fight that already broke Monday’s shared camera coverage.

stories.title: Google backs Georgia Power nuclear uprates (~96 MW)
facts: POWER Magazine (Sep 21): Google and Georgia Power agree Google will support extended power uprates at Plant Vogtle and Plant Hatch — about 96 MW of added nuclear capacity if approved.
Georgia PSC approval still needed; utility filed for a new NU-1 nuclear-uprate tariff; Google would subscribe and receive zero-emission credits tied to the uprate output.
Georgia Power projects roughly $900 million in customer benefits over the life of the units; Hatch EPU request filed Monday; Vogtle 1–2 EPU already approved in the 2025 IRP.
CNA/business wires carry the Southern Co. unit framing the same deal.
stories.whyItMatters: Another hyperscaler bet on squeezing more MWs from existing U.S. reactors — billed as grid capacity for data-center growth with shared customer benefits.

stories.title: EU auditors: bloc still poorly prepared for major cyber incidents
facts: heise: European Court of Auditors special report says EU action only partially helps detect and respond to significant/large-scale cyber incidents — information-sharing gaps are the biggest weakness.

ECA Facts & Findings (SR 19/2026): calls to enhance information-sharing and cut task overlap, make the European Cybersecurity Alert System operational, and tighten security assessment/monitoring for EU-funded entities.

Auditors cite the Sep 2025 airport IT outage: Germany, Belgium and Ireland did not notify ENISA/peers as expected, leaving joint response tools unused; national-security carve-outs still block sharing.
stories.whyItMatters: An official EU audit, not a vendor white paper — documenting that cross-border incident response still fails under national-security exceptions.

stories.title: Paramount clears state/WGA hurdles; Warner close pressed toward end-Sep
facts: heise: Paramount Skydance settles with 12 U.S. states and the Writers Guild, clearing antitrust suits that stood in the way of buying Warner Bros. Discovery.
Deal terms cited: ~$31/share for Warner (~$81B equity; ~$111B including debt/obligations); close targeted for end of September.
From Oct 1, Paramount faced ~$7M/day contractual penalties to Warner if the deal slipped — a hard deadline after Monday’s settlements.

State deal includes five-year film/streaming commitments (Pluto TV, U.S. production floors, indie spend, news editorial independence board for CNN/CBS); WGA suit to be dropped with reported health-fund/job assurances.
stories.whyItMatters: The last big courtroom blockers are bargained away just as daily reverse-termination pressure kicks in — the megadeal’s closing window is now measured in days.
